OPER A T I O N A L

 ISSUANCE DATE                 SUBJECT(S): TR 8 Progress Inspections, TR8 Inspections Reports,
   April 3, 2025                           Approved Inspection Agencies, Progress Inspectors



     RELATED CODE SECTIONS & RESOURCES
     1 RCNY 5000-01, 1 RCNY 101-07 and 2020 NYC Energy Conservation Code


  I. BACKGROUND
     TR8 progress inspections are an integral part of ensuring compliance with the New York City Energy
     Conservation Code. The Approved Progress Inspection Agency maintains responsibility for the
     inspection and accurate reporting of Energy Code verifications during all required phases of construction
     activity. 1-RCNY 101-07 Section (b) (9) authorizes the Department to Audit “The operations of Approved
     Agencies.“ This bulletin clarifies the requirements for submittal to the Department for audit of records
     upon request.


  II. SUBMITTALS
     Progress Inspection Reports shall be submitted by the Approved Progress Inspection Agency, at the
     request of the Department, with documentation of each unique inspection as defined in 1 RCNY 101.7
     (c)(3)(v)(C).
     Documentation must include, but is not limited to, time, date, and subject of inspection, a detailed
     description of the assembly, equipment, or test being reported, reference to the drawing detail or
     specification being verified, and date stamped photo-documentation of each unique condition observed.
     Guidelines are available at https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/energy-conservation-
     code.page for reference to Progress Inspection reporting requirements .


  III. SCHEDULE
     Approved Inspection Agent shall submit Progress Inspection Reports during construction. At regular
     intervals, described below, the Agent shall submit all inspections completed to date to: TR8inspections
     (Buildings) TR8inspections@buildings.nyc.gov.

     Progress Inspection Reports shall be submitted for review:
     1) Prior to completing the enclosure of exterior cladding, brick veneer, EIFS, or panelized systems of
        the thermal Envelope.

         A3 - Fenestration u-factor and product rating
         A4 - Fenestration air leakage
         A7 - Air barrier testing or A8 - Air barrier continuity plan testing (as applicable)
         B2 - Shutoff dampers (Commercial) or Ventilation and air distribution system (residential)
         B3 - HVAC-R and service water heating equipment
         B4 - HVAC-R and service water heating system controls
         B5 - HVAC-R and service water piping design and insulation
         B6 - Duct leakage testing, insulation, and design

     3) At the completion of Mechanical and Lighting systems installation prior to painting and finishes.
         These Inspections typically include:
         C1 - Metering
         C2 - Lighting in dwelling units (Commercial) or Interior lighting power (Residential)
         C3 - Interior lighting power
         C4 - Exterior lighting power
         C5 - Lighting controls
         C6 - Electrical motors and elevators
         D1 - Maintenance information
         D2 - Permanent certificate (Residential)
         D3 - Electric vehicle service equipment requirements (Residential)
         B2 - Ventilation and air distribution system (as applicable for controls)
         B6 - Duct leakage testing, insulation, and design (as applicable for controls)



   IV. ACCEPTANCE & CONTINUATION OF WORK
      Progress Inspection Reports may be audited and subject to clarification. The Approved Inspection
      Agent shall remain responsible for certification of site conditions. Should the Department audit reveal
      deficiencies in the as-built conditions, or discrepancies in Progress Inspection Reports, the
      Commissioner shall reserve the right to Stop Work and order remedy of same.
